description: ALLFED's integrated Python model tests how food systems could respond to severe shocks, including nuclear-winter crop losses. It combines country food production, feed and biofuel allocation, trade choices and resilient-food options in successive optimisation rounds. Users choose scenario YAML files and country or global assumptions; outputs include monthly food availability, calories and shares of people fed under the modelled choices. The README illustrates an Argentina no-trade scenario, while other country codes can be selected. Temporal resolution is monthly in those result plots; geographic resolution is by country, not individual farms. GPL-3.0 source and scenario examples are freely available. The repository describes a conda environment and rerun commands, but this metadata review did not execute them. Results depend heavily on assumed shock severity, input data, diet, trade and adaptation options; the output is a conditional scenario, not an observed famine forecast. The model serves food-supply resilience and emergency planning. The catalogue's model-agrifoodpy is a separate food-system model for comparison, with no verified interface. No model archive or input data was downloaded.
